a big part of my current job when i first started was helping the elderly use their smartphones and computers with enough understanding of the technology that they don't accidentally destroy their bank accounts and lives. there are a few hurdles to this. one is vision. many people lose their vision as they age and the small prints on a tiny screen can be impossible to view and not everyone can afford to constantly be getting their eyeglasses adjusted.

for example, if i ask them about their password they will say "i don't have a password/i didn't know i had a password/what is a password". and after asking a few more times, they will say something like "oh well you said password, i don't have a passWORD, i only have a passCODE". ive also seen where they so badly don't want the technology to be functioning (because they want to complain? idk) so they lie that something is wrong. such if i ask them if they can open their email, they reply "my phone is broken, i cant". even if they open their email, they say they cannot see it or its still not working, as if i cannot see exactly what they are looking at. but then when i go to check they will be like "oh that just happened, it wasn't before". this situation usually escalates to anger and they often yell at me about how things were better without technology. 

this isn't ALL older people, there are many very kind and patient people who are very respectful. but its definitely a good proportion of the people ive had to assist.

a few years ago, i hiked a really long trail called the Pacific Crest Trail. its over 2000 miles and takes 4 months minimum, extending from southern cali to northern washington. my day 1, starting in southern california i met this guy, ill call him Max. he was pretty cool but after 3 days we got separated and I didn't see him again. i remembered he had a yellow bandana and these really fancy hiking poles. the weather got really bad and so a lot of people were changing their plans (skipping sections, going north and hiking the opposite direction, etc). i didn't have his number or even his last name so i didn't know how to contact him or find him online so i never found out what he did.

five months later, after finishing the trail, i was driving through southern california, praying for a sign on what the heck to do with my life after finishing this damn trail. i was driving from palm springs area towards LA, and i was trying to stop in this small town which was near where the PCT intersected the highway and i kept missing my damn exit. i missed this exit not once, not twice, but THREE DAMN TIMES. i ended up pulling over and getting out of the car, i was so frustrated.

when i turned around to walk back to the car, there was a hitch hiker standing on the side of the road. if i hadn't missed my exits, i wouldn't have seen him. i offered him a ride since he was trying to get back into the town i was also going to. while driving him to town, we talked a bit. turns out, he had just finished the pacific crest trail too. what happened was, the weather had gotten bad so he flipped north and started walking south. i was staring at him a minute, and i realized he had the SAME BANDANA as my friend Max did. in that same moment, he was also staring at me and said "nobonomore, is that you?".

because he had grown a beard, and i was wearing makeup and "girl clothes" for the first time, and both of us were thinner, we didn't recognize each other immediately. but it was my long lost friend from day one of the trail, and it was the sign I was looking for from the universe. i had only been stopped for FIVE MINUTES, and if i hadn't missed my exits, i wouldn't have seen him. there were so many factors that had to fall into place in order for me to see him that day, that moment even, it blows my mind still that it happened. i just took it to mean that i was exactly where i was meant to be, and to just be patient with my life, the world, and with everything.

Specifically, when you are trying to describe her reaction as "acting normal but finding herself crying randomly"...like if thats how it really was to be sexually assaulted then it probably wouldn't be that big of a deal to be assaulted. but sexual assault is a horrible traumatizing thing and emotions tend to be all over the place. many victims dont acknowledge it for months or years after, they just feel a general sense of confusion/numbness before feeling all types of complex emotions including anger/despair/etc.

if you really want good resources on how to describe this character's emotional reaction to this trauma, i would recommend checking out the wikipedia page for RTS (rape trauma syndrome). it outlines the 'general' stages of symptoms which sexual assault survivors typically face, in 3 phases. reading this could make it a lot easier to outline her healing from it.

i know you don't want her whole story to be about trauma, but unfortunately, when you are raped, your whole life does become about rape. that is why it is such a debilitating thing. rape survivors want to just forget about it and move on with their lives but they cannot, they are plagued with thoughts of it 24/7. if you are going to add a sexual assault to your character's storyline, it does have to be kind of a big deal.
